exact_factor_and_singular_scheme_audit.boundary_geometric_integrality_argument: If the F5-irreducible sextic split into r>=2 equal-degree Frobenius components, every F5-rational singular center would lie on all of them. Two components would share ten points, contradicting Bezout because their common degree 6/r is at most three.

exact_factor_and_singular_scheme_audit.hostile_warning: The boundary does not have ten nodes. Its saturated Jacobian scheme has length 16 and is nonreduced at the six A2 cusps; only its radical is the reduced ten-center scheme.
exact_factor_and_singular_scheme_audit.quartic_geometric_integrality_argument: F5-irreducibility makes geometric components a Frobenius orbit. Ordinary nodes force at most two components. Two conjugate conics would meet transversely at the three rational nodes, so Bezout forces a fourth intersection and hence another singular point, contrary to the exact three-point singular scheme.
